## What I did

I could not read your local `phix174.fasta`. The only filesystem access I have in this session is Galaxy's `upload_file`, and it reported "File not found" for `phix174.fasta` in the working directory and every other path I tried (`data/`, home, scratchpad). There is no shell or file-read tool available to me here.

So I ran the analysis on the reference phiX174 genome from NCBI — **NC_001422.1**, *Escherichia* phage phiX174, complete genome, 5386 bp — fetched via NCBI E-utilities into Galaxy (usegalaxy.org, v26.1), history `bbd44e69cb8906b51f139dda1a7db940`, dataset `f9cad7b01a472135554b78ad9635b420`. Galaxy confirmed 1 sequence, 79 lines, 5520 bytes. **If your file is a subregion, a different isolate, or carries engineered changes, this result does not necessarily apply to it** — tell me a readable path and I'll rerun on the actual file.

**Tool:** EMBOSS `fuzznuc` 5.0.3, exact match (`-pmismatch 0`), both strands (`-complement yes`).

| Enzyme | Site | Hits | Dataset / job |
|---|---|---|---|
| EcoRI | GAATTC | **0** | `f9cad7b01a472135d7044512a0de9293` / job `bbd44e69cb8906b59ad6e45b57705196`, exit 0 |
| BamHI | GGATCC | **0** | `f9cad7b01a47213516ac756395f38f27` / job `bbd44e69cb8906b50cff027fe43ba2b4`, exit 0 |

**Positive control** (because two empty outputs are exactly what a silently broken run looks like): same tool, `GAATTC` with 1 mismatch returned 20 positions per strand / 40 rows (dataset `f9cad7b01a4721358e68b76a86946486`) — e.g. 81–86, 102–107, 4535–4540. The search machinery and pattern syntax work, so the zeros are real.

**Circular junction checked.** phiX174 is circular, and `fuzznuc` on a linear FASTA cannot see a site spanning position 5386→1. I pulled the last line of the FASTA (`Select last`, dataset `f9cad7b01a4721356c28cb54454536c0`): the genome ends `...GATTGGCGTATCCAACCTGCA` and begins `GAGTTTTATCGCTTCC...`, giving the junction `...CCAACCTGCA|GAGTTTTATC...`. No GAATTC and no GGATCC there either. (That junction does contain `CTGCAG` — phiX174's well-known single PstI site, which is precisely why the junction was worth checking.)

## One practical note on the cloning itself

The flip side of zero internal sites is that there are also **no EcoRI or BamHI sites anywhere in this sequence at all**, including at the ends. You'll need to add them — standard approach is tailed PCR primers carrying `GAATTC` and `GGATCC` plus a few spacer bases. Dam methylation is not a concern: BamHI is insensitive to it.

## ANSWER

**No. Neither enzyme cuts inside the fragment — your EcoRI/BamHI cloning is safe.**

- EcoRI (GAATTC): 0 sites
- BamHI (GGATCC): 0 sites

Both strands, exact match, plus the circular 5386→1 junction, all clear. Source: NCBI **NC_001422.1** (5386 bp), analyzed with EMBOSS `fuzznuc` 5.0.3 on usegalaxy.org — **not** your local `phix174.fasta`, which I had no way to read.
